title: AI model
short: The program that writes Copilot’s answers.
body: The program that writes Copilot’s answers. It learned patterns from huge amounts of text and code, and predicts a useful reply to what you send. Copilot lets you choose between several models.
analogy: A very well-read colleague who has never seen your project.

title: Prompt
body: What you type to Copilot: a question, a task or an instruction. The clearer it is, the fewer rounds you need.
analogy: The brief you give a contractor.

title: Context
short: Everything the model sees when it answers.
body: Everything Copilot sends to the model with your prompt: the chat so far, files you attach, instruction files and tool results. The model only knows what is in the context. It has no other memory of your project.
analogy: A whiteboard. Whatever is written on it is all the model can see.

title: Token
short: The chunk of text models read and bill in.
body: The unit models read, and the unit usage is measured in. A token is a chunk of text, often part of a word: in English, a token is roughly three-quarters of a word on average. Code and symbols usually take more.
analogy: Syllables. Long or unusual words take several.

title: Context window
short: The most context a model can take at once.
body: The most context a model can take in one request, measured in tokens. As a chat nears the limit, older parts get summarised or dropped and answers get worse.

title: Chat history
short: Every prompt and reply in the current chat.
body: Every prompt and reply in the current chat. It is sent again with each new prompt, which is why long chats get slower and cost more.
analogy: Rereading the whole email thread before every reply.

title: Agent
body: A Copilot role that doesn’t just answer. It works out the steps, edits files, runs commands and checks the results, repeating until the task is done or it needs you.
analogy: A junior developer you supervise, rather than a search engine.

title: Tool
short: An action an agent can take.
body: An action an agent can take, such as reading a file, searching the code, running a terminal command or fetching a web page. Whatever a tool returns is added to the context.

title: Hallucination
short: A confident answer that is wrong.
body: A confident answer that is wrong, such as a function, setting or package that doesn’t exist. Models predict likely text. They don’t check facts unless a tool, a test or you do.
analogy: A colleague bluffing instead of saying “I don’t know”.

title: AI credits
body: How Copilot measures usage: each request costs credits based on the model and the tokens used. Bigger models and bigger contexts cost more.
analogy: A phone plan billed by the minute, where some numbers cost more to call.

title: Instruction file
short: Team rules Copilot adds to every request.
body: A Markdown file in your repo, such as .github/copilot-instructions.md, whose rules Copilot adds to requests automatically. You write the team’s conventions once instead of in every prompt.
analogy: The onboarding notes you hand every new starter.

title: Inline suggestion
short: Grey ghost text offered as you type.
body: The grey “ghost text” Copilot offers as you type in the editor. Press Tab to accept it, or keep typing to ignore it.
analogy: Autocomplete on your phone, for whole lines of code.

title: Compaction
short: Shrinking the chat into a short summary.
body: Replacing a long chat history with a short summary, so it takes fewer tokens. /compact does it when you ask; VS Code also does it automatically when the window fills.
analogy: Wiping the whiteboard but keeping a sticky note of the key points.

title: Diff
short: A before-and-after view of a change.
body: A view of exactly what changed in a file: removed lines and added lines. Reading the diff is how you check Copilot’s work before you keep it.
analogy: Tracked changes in a Word document.

title: MCP server
short: An add-on that gives the agent extra tools.
body: An add-on that gives the agent extra tools, such as access to a database, an issue tracker or a browser. MCP stands for Model Context Protocol.
analogy: A plug-in adapter that lets the agent use one more system.
